The fog comes first, red and thick, pouring out of the trees until the torches on the far wall are only smudges.

Then the screeching starts, from everywhere at once.

The first Screecher comes over the palisade on all fours, one arm hanging by a strip of skin. It does not seem to notice. An arrow takes it in the chest and it keeps coming.

To the left a conscript screams as claws open his thigh. Halena drags him back from the parapet and shoves a spear into the gap.

Below the wall a Screecher falls, and falls apart: it bubbles into the mud like wax, and where it lay a scatter of white flowers opens in the dark.

Somewhere down the line a defender stops shooting and stares into the fog, and the thing climbing toward him has a face he knows.

The fog is still thick, and dawn is hours away.

Bashima's symbol is a blazing staff and followers typically carry a wooden token or walking cane as a mark of faith.
Appearance: depicted as a six-armed woman in travelling robes, each hand holding a different road or household tool, hearth-flame halo.

Dalan is amazing with a bow, hates being called cute, and has his own 'fan club' which has apparently sworn to protect him. Dalan is friends with Ellie and Jasira. Dalan is a member of the Evergreen Tribe of Elves which are located in Duskwallow Forest.

Fiana Deulana is a young woman who works in the Adventurers Guild's Tavern at Aegis City. Fiana has short, curly red hair, huge breasts, freckles, blue eyes, and is about average height. Fiana is known for being an extrovert, often drinking with adventurers. Fiana is one of the "Jewels of the Guild" in Aegis City according to fanclubs.
Appearance: young woman, human, shoulder-length red hair, white maid headdress, blue eyes, black puff-sleeved bolero, blue and red corset dress with bow and blue gem brooch.

Rydel Deulana is a male beastfolk with dog heritage, blue hair, green eyes, and a tall build. Rydel is Fiana's adopted brother. Rydel works as the bartender at the Aegis City Adventurers Guild Tavern and is well-liked by the patrons who visit because of his charming and earnest demeanor. Rydel is considered one of the "Jewels of the Adventurers Guild."
Appearance: adult man, dog beastfolk, floppy blue dog ears, long messy blue hair, green eyes, white open-collar shirt, dark teal vest, silver chain necklace with pendant.

worldBook.comment: Hianxo - Capital of the Third Kingdom
worldBook.text:
Hianxo is the Capital of the Third Kingdom
Appearance: Massive capital city, feudal Japanese-style pagodas and tiled-roof teahouses, timber and stone, pink cherry blossoms and red lacquer, warm lantern glow, Jiansho Academy.

The Third Kingdom is a dynasty ruled by Emperor Zhao who maintains a strict rule over the Third Kingdom located on the eastern continent of Savalon (citizens are called Savalonians). The Third Kingdom maintains peaceful relations with the Darran Kingdom through a military alliance. The Third Kingdom's capital is Hianxo. Savalonian citizens practice a strict "Warrior Culture" based on personal honor. Savalonians tend to worship a variety of minor deities. Third Kingdom tea is said to be the best in the world.
Appearance: eastern realm of Savalon, terraced green hills and tea fields, curved tiled roofs, red lacquer gates, the walled capital of Hianxo.

Warchief Wurgoth Oxtusk is the leader of the Zegallan Empire. Wurgoth is a brute of an Orc with a sadistic streak to match.
Appearance: massive orc man, grey-green skin, heavy lower tusks, shaved scarred scalp, red eyes, spiked black iron plate, fur mantle, great axe.

The Zegallan Empire is a warlike empire founded after it's citizens defeated their lizardfolk overlords almost a century ago. The Zegallan's leader is Warchief Wurgoth. The Zegallan Empire believe the weak should serve the strong and has a slavery system in place. Zegallan's capitol is Nuwerth City. The Zegallan Empires primary deity is Prodyr, God of Fire and War.
Appearance: warlike empire of red rock and ash plains, fortified black-stone holds, banners of flame, forge smoke, the walled capital of Nuwerth.

[State of the war in this campaign. The Zegallan Empire's surprise attacks have taken footholds in the Darran Kingdom; the Cursefire Regiment holds the western front and the Kelnan survivors are being sold in Nuwerth. The Crown has not yet called a muster.]

[Group members, who speak and act for themselves: Belle, a tall muscular human barbarian with long black hair and a greataxe called Cleaver, blunt and loud; Dalan Evergreen, a short slender blond elf ranger with a shortbow, shy and observant; Honami Nemaden, a three-tailed kitsune onmyoji of Jiansho Academy called the Charming Beast, long white hair over her right eye, red eyes, a red, black and white qipao, the party's guide in the Third Kingdom and fixed on {{story_player_name}}; Hanzo Hattaxi, a tall scarred ninja of the Hattaxi Clan in black and red ninja-yoroi with katana and wakizashi, cocky and proud, who ends up escorting the party inland. Cameos join for their scenes: in Hianxo Megumi Xianxu, Tanya Hattaxi and Rikako Kagamihi; on the road the oni Hanabi and Shinen; in Tiunhime the villagers and its three gods, Ebisu, Watara and Yurine.]

[Scene state: the harbour of Hianxo, capital of the Third Kingdom, late morning. Tall-masted ships from across the Jehopa Ocean, fish markets, teahouses, red lacquer gates climbing toward Jiansho Academy's pagoda roofs, cherry blossom falling. The party has just landed with the Academy's invitation to the Jiansho Tournament. Honami Nemaden is waiting to guide them.]

The citizenry of the Third Kingdom (Savalonians) all serve the Emperor (Emperor Zhao). Many citizens of the Third Kingdom enjoy the native drink of Sake (alcohol produced from fermented rice) and tea culture is prominent in the Third Kingdom, with some of the best tea masters in the world living in Hianxo. The Third Kingdom fosters a "Warrior Culture" in it's people where citizens are encouraged to follow an Honor Code that emphasizes personal honor. Wearing masks that represent animal spirits or even yokai is popular in the Third Kingdom as a form of self-expression. Spirituality and reverence to the many spirits (often taking the form of animals) that wander Savalon is an important facet of life in the Third Kingdom. Clothes in the third kingdom are often Haori, Yukata, and Kimono which are layered robes for various occasions originally developed in the Third Kingdom. Many individual villages set up shrines to local Gods and practice unique customs and traditions in their daily lives. Copper, Silver, and Gold coins are used as currency in Savalon. Savalonian homes tend to be made of stone in the city or Wood/Tatami in rural villages. Respect for elders is a big part of Savalonian society.
Appearance: Vast continent, forested hills and mountain ranges, pagoda shrines and timber villages, pink cherry blossom groves, soft misty light, Guao peaks piercing clouds.

worldBook.comment: Deep - The Tear Over the Altar
worldBook.text: [What happened at Carrow Keep. Lord Aldric Carrow bought branded captives from the Beastmen of Nahalbuk under his keep and bled them on his altar to tear a hole in the planes and call a demon to make him immortal. It came, and ate him. His armoured guards were changed by it: inky tentacles through the joints of their plate, no longer men. The tear above the altar still weeps violet light and demon-reek, and it has been smelled from very far below.]

[Unira Windsor, a short, strong young human woman with long silver hair and dark red eyes, a Fighter of the Aegis City Guild listed as dead. A middle child of the Windsor family, who serve House Nightriver; she ran away to adventure with sword and shield. Reserved, slow to trust, kind, quick to cuss, sure she is never good enough. Terrified of Beastmen since her captivity; a blade scar on her left arm.]

[Dungeon Nahalbuk is a new dungeon under Carrow Keep, home to a Beastmen tribe whose shaman sold captives up the stair. Before a sacrifice, captives receive the Tahanna Brand, a trident with a coiled snake, set on the soul: the branded must stay near the brand's owner and obey their commands, resisting only at great pain, and cannot speak of the brand or harm the owner. It glows purple while a command is working. Removing it usually kills. If the owner is killed, the brand passes to the killer.]

[What Unira told. Her party, the Wind Ballad (Kallan, a human fighter she had feelings for; Fulanie, a half-elf ice mage; Mallow, a halfling cleric of Boher), took a D-rank scouting job into Nahalbuk when it was new and were overrun by Beastmen. Mallow said to leave her behind, Kallan shoved her into the horde and Fulanie froze her boots to the floor. They reported to the Guild that she volunteered to hold the line and died. She was captured and branded instead.]

[At the Draxford mine camp: Amthir and Nendira Draxford, the drow heir and heiress of House Draxford, tall, dark grey skin, black hair over one eye, red eyes, one shoulder bare in the Draxford style, earth mages and longbow archers, blunt, done with court manners. Hired adventurers answering the muster: Anax and Sana, silver-haired elven sorcerers in wide black hats, once middle-rank, now called the Mana-less Mage and the Spell-less Mage; Shadur and Shelur, tall green-skinned orc druids of the Helioth Circle in feathered cloaks, cheerful, who wear no metal.]

[What the Draxfords know. Terrorborn are massive insectoids out of the deep Darklands with hard chitin: drones the size of wagons and swarms small enough to choke on. They do not crawl out of caves, they burst up out of the rock. They drag people alive into their hives. They seek demon flesh, and nobody knows why. Draxford lands are the only lands in the Kingdom hit by them every year; this breach runs from the lower workings toward Carrow Keep.]

worldBook.text: [World: Adolion. Centuries ago the undead Lich Queen conquered the continent of Sebela; only Aegis City, capital of the human Darran Kingdom, held out behind its holy shield until a band of adventurers slew her. Her freed undead still roam, necromancer sects plot her return, and her servant the Witch King lies sealed, not destroyed. Peoples are recovering and settling beyond the walls, but the wilds teem with monsters and rival powers, so the Adventuring Doctrine founded the Adventurer's Guild, which ranks adventurers and posts quests for coin. The fire-worshipping Zegallan Empire wars with both the Darran Kingdom and the Third Kingdom of Savalon. Flintlocks, gunpowder and magic-lifted airships exist alongside swords and spells.]

A Slave Crest is a magical mark on a slaves body that binds them to their 'Master.' Slaves who defy orders or try to harm their master will slowly be killed by the crest until they obey. Some Masters prefer to use collars instead of a mark.

The Zegallan Empire has four types of slaves: Indentured Slaves who became slaves to pay off debts, Special Slaves who sell themselves into slavery, Wartime Slaves, and Criminal Slaves. Slavery in Zegallan is seen as a noble undertaking where even the lowest dregs of society can redeem themselves. Everywhere else, it's considered an evil practice.

The Zegallan Empire is a warlike empire founded after it's citizens defeated their lizardfolk overlords almost a century ago. The Zegallan's leader is Warchief Wurgoth. The Zegallan Empire believe the weak should serve the strong and has a slavery system in place. Zegallan's capitol is Nuwerth City. The Zegallan Empires primary deity is Prodyr, God of Fire and War.
Appearance: warlike empire of red rock and ash plains, fortified black-stone holds, banners of flame, forge smoke, the walled capital of Nuwerth.

[State of the war in this campaign. The Zegallan Empire's surprise attacks have taken footholds in the Darran Kingdom; the Cursefire Regiment holds the western front and the Kelnan survivors are being sold in Nuwerth. The Crown has not yet called a muster.]

The War between the Zegallan Empire and the Darran Kingdom is not going well. The Zegallan Empire's might is formidable and the Darran Kingdom is constantly losing ground which is not helped by constant infighting of the noble houses.

[Group members, who speak and act for themselves: Belle, a tall muscular human barbarian with long black hair and a greataxe called Cleaver, headstrong and loyal; Dalan Evergreen, a slight blond elf ranger of the Evergreen Tribe with a shortbow, shy and sharp-eyed. The Darran court, who speak for themselves when present: King Alexander Davolan, the Warrior King, 47, short silver hair and beard, a gold crown with a red gem, formal, cunning and vindictive; Crown Prince Forre, 23, silver hair and green eyes, blademaster and tactician in blue and silver, who commands the field army; Crown Princess Haley, 21, long silver hair and green eyes, a peerless fencer devoted to her mother; Queen Melisande, 42, silver hair in a bun held by a Third Kingdom pin, one yellow eye and one purple, born a Zhao, an exorcist; Vallie Goredust, Guildmaster, a one-eyed minotaur woman with red hair and horns, veteran of the last Zegallan war.]

[The war as the Darran Kingdom knows it. The Zegallan Empire, fire-worshipping and ruled by Warchief Wurgoth from Nuwerth in western Sebela, resumed the war with surprise attacks that took the border fortress-town of Greywater and the villages of the Ashen March. The Cursefire Regiment holds Greywater under Kanna Helfin, the Blood Saint. Fort Vicinitas, which held in the last war, is the Darran strongpoint on the ridge opposite. Behind the Darran line a winged herald of Prodyr burns villages. Zegallan raiders carry captives west as slaves. The dead of both sides have been vanishing from the burial pits at the front; the court blames the Queen's Cult, and the whispers name Queen Melisande.]

[The Zegallan enemy at the front. Kanna Helfin, the Blood Saint, who speaks for herself: a tall demonborn woman of 25 with short wavy blood-red hair and dark red eyes, in blackened plate she summons in a swirl of blood, with the greataxe Blood Oath; a vulgar, battle-hungry blood mage who worships Prodyr, executes cowards, and keeps her word. Her Cursefire Regiment fights with cannon and firearms behind a drugged, frenzied slave corps, and its Demon Squad are flesh-shaped monsters twice a man's height.]

[Scene state: Fort Vicinitas on its ridge above the Ashen March, the burned country in front of it and Greywater's walls across the valley under the Cursefire banner. Cannon at dawn, raids at night; the Darran shield walls hold the ridge.]

Domas Syllandri is the Vice Guildmaster of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild and former party member of "Will of Steel", a retired A-Rank Adventuring Party. Domas is an elven man with blonde hair, red eyes, a tall and well-toned build, and admittedly "Quite attractive" according to wistful bards. worldBook.comment: Vallie Goredust - Guildmaster of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild
worldBook.text:
Vallie Goredust or "Deathaxe" is the Guildmaster of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild and former Party Leader for "Will of Steel", a retired A-rank Adventuring Party. Vallie is a Beastfolk woman with minotaur heritage, with shaggy red hair, a missing eye, a blue eye, huge breasts, a very tall muscular build, and ox horns on her head. Vallie is the one who implemented rank requirements for taking quests, which has drastically reduced casualty rates. Vallie is a good-natured woman, if a bit crass and intimidating.
Appearance: adult woman, muscular, long red hair in ponytail, curved black horns, blue eye, black eyepatch, scars, sharp teeth, brown leather bustier, spiked black pauldron, leather bracers, dark trousers, brown boots.

[Scene state: the Adventurer's Guild hall in Aegis City, midday. Tobias works the quest counter with Ellie Sunleaf beside him; Guildmaster Vallie Goredust's office door stands open upstairs, and the Guild tavern is through the arch next door. The posting that matters is D-rank, Investigate Wendhope: the mining village on Sheridan lands has sent no ore for weeks and neighbouring Raltdorf has heard nothing from it.
